title: Building Doors with Integrated Location-Based Emergency Call Functionality
content: The aim of this study is to explore how to shorten firefighter search time during indoor fires to rescue more people, through enhancing disaster prevention capabilities with building technologies. In indoor fires, fatalities are often caused by the failure of firefighters to rescue individuals in a timely manner. How to effectively increase the probability of survival while waiting for rescue behind closed doors warrants in-depth research and analysis. Therefore, to ensure that people live in a safe environment, there is an urgent need for a building door panel material with an emergency call function to prevent such incidents from occurring. By utilizing the PRISMA method, the authors conducted a comprehensive review of existing literature to identify the key issues and limitations associated with the current search and rescue techniques. Subsequently, the identified primary factors were analyzed using the TRIZ method to determine the key factors influencing the success of rescuing trapped individuals, and a notification system was designed to address this issue. Based on the premise that it is advisable to wait for rescue during a fire, we utilize a smartphone to scan a QR code and transmit the exact location information to the fire department. Through extensive participation and feedback from firefighters, the author has developed a rescue notification door panel and has obtained a patent for it. This system can significantly reduce the time required for search and rescue operations in fire incidents. The experimental results show a reduction of one-third in search time.
